James Gunn recently hosted a screening of *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2* and shared some fascinating behind-the-scenes insights. Here’s a curated look at the most intriguing details:

- The 1980 film Flash Gordon was a major source of visual inspiration for the director while crafting the movie’s tone and aesthetic.  
- On set, Kurt Russell repeatedly called Chris Pratt’s character “Star Wars” instead of “Star-Lord”—a flub that stuck as an ongoing joke.  
- Costume designers spent a significant amount of time perfecting Ayesha’s gown. Gunn considers it one of the most striking elements in the entire film.  
- He particularly loves the comedic chemistry between Chris Pratt and Dave Bautista, calling their dynamic effortless and electric.  
- Gunn wanted to humanize Nebula, who was originally a villain in the first film. To do that, he focused on her relationship with Gamora, framing them as sisters with a painful shared history.  
- Making the film helped Pratt process the loss of his father—an experience he found emotionally grounding.  
- The young alien girl from the Kree race? That’s Grace Gunn, James Gunn’s real-life niece.  
- Rocket’s decision to build a bomb with two buttons instead of one? It was intentional—because the device had multiple purposes.  
- Gunn praised Chris Pratt’s growth as an actor, noting his performance deepened significantly in the sequel.  
- Dave Bautista’s reaction to Ego’s “decent-sized” penis had Gunn literally falling off his chair laughing.  
- The most challenging scene to shoot was Ego’s monologue about his past. The sheer amount of exposition made it tough to keep emotionally engaging.  
- During the final battle with Ego, Pratt fell from a height of 4.5 meters, hit his head, and briefly lost consciousness—a moment that shocked the crew.  
- Kraglin’s triumphant scream at the end was inspired by Christopher Lloyd’s iconic cry in One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest.  
- One of Gunn’s all-time favorite scenes he’s ever directed? Yondu’s escape sequence—pure cinematic adrenaline.  
- He joked, “Has Baby Yoda ever killed people as brutally as Baby Groot did in the Escape Pod scene?”  
- Baby Groot antagonizes Drax throughout the film—but chooses him in the end, revealing he actually loves him the most.  
- Peter Quill’s emotional final speech over Yondu’s body was constantly interrupted by Michael Rooker’s snoring—since he was lying in the coffin.  
- Gunn confirmed that the scene featuring the remains of Ego’s children is packed with Easter eggs, some still undiscovered.  
- The fight between Gamora and Nebula was directly inspired by the plane sequence in the thriller North by Northwest.  
- Pom Klementieff was, in Gunn’s words, “born to play Mantis.” He can’t imagine anyone else in the role—and teases that her future arc will surprise us all.  
- When Rocket says, “Today I can only afford to lose one friend,” he’s referring to Yondu—because he knows Yondu plans to save Quill, at his own cost.

How to check which services you accessed through Apple ID and Google, and not lose access to them

From July 6, Russian websites and applications are required to remove the "Sign in with Google/Apple" buttons. The accounts themselves are not deleted, but access to them can be lost.

To prevent this from happening, you need to find the profiles created with Apple ID and Google, and add new ways to log in to them:
🍏 For Apple ID

On iPhone, iPad, or Mac, go to "Settings" → your name → "Sign in with Apple".

Here you can see all the applications and services that you accessed through Apple ID, as well as the substitute emails from the "Hide email" feature - save these addresses, you can use them to log in as well.
🔎 For Google Account

From any device and browser, go to myaccount.google.com/connections.

Here you can see all the applications and services where login was set up through Google.

Now log in to the necessary services through Apple/Google and add alternative login methods, such as by phone.

Authorities waited more than four months — until a cease-fire with Washington was in place — before risking a mass event with all the regime’s senior brass in one place. 

Analysts say the delay was about security, but it also reflects anxiety: you don’t pack the entire power structure into a funeral hall while U.S. and Israeli missiles are still in the air.

On camera, it’s a show of strength: millions expected on the streets, foreign delegations flying in from across the region, and wall‑to‑wall coverage on state TV. 

The succession looks less like transition and more like inheritance. His son, Mojtaba Khamenei, has already been named supreme leader and promptly disappeared from public view, while the same security, clerical, and business networks remain bolted into place. 

Even inside the loyalist camp, the funeral is not a unifying ritual. Hard‑liners accuse the leadership of selling out by signing a cease-fire with the U.S., asking on banners, “What happened to revenge for the blood of our martyred Imam?” — turning a state funeral into a passive‑aggressive referendum on whether the regime is still revolutionary enough for its own base.

From the outside, Washington and Jerusalem didn’t get regime change; they got a wounded system trying to prove it can absorb a direct decapitation strike and keep marching. 

From the inside, many Iranians are watching the most expensive funeral in the country’s history while inflation, corruption, and repression keep grinding on — proof that even in death, the supreme leader still gets VIP treatment, and everyone else gets the bill.

❗️ XRP price forms multi-month falling wedge near $1 support as liquidations mount 

📣 According to data from cryptonews price, XRP price dropped from around $1.07 on June 25 to $1.01 on June 26, extending its year-to-date decline to more than 40%. The decline accelerated as a $10.8 billion crypto options expiry triggered heavy volatility across digital assets and forced a wave of long liquidations.

⚠️ At the same time, sentiment surrounding the XRP ecosystem weakened after decentralized finance protocol Strobe Finance abruptly announced it would shut down operations.

🔖 The daily chart shows XRP trading at the lower edge of a falling wedge that has contained price action for almost a year. The pattern has compressed between descending resistance and gradually declining support, with the token now sitting close to the wedge’s lower boundary near $1.00.

🔗 Momentum indicators remain weak. The MACD has stayed below its signal line with histogram bars still in negative territory, while the Aroon indicator continues to favor sellers after Aroon Down climbed back toward 100 and Aroon Up remained subdued. Together, the indicators suggest bears still control the short-term trend even as XRP price approaches a historically important support zone.
